title: hnscc-tls-signatures: analysis code and derived data for "Tertiary lymphoid structure gene signatures are not interchangeable in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma"
description:
Reproducible analysis pipeline, derived patient-level data, and complete result tables and figures for the manuscript "Tertiary lymphoid structure gene signatures are not interchangeable in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a retrospective multi-signature transcriptomic analysis" (submitted to Journal of Translational Medicine).

Study summary. Chemokine-based transcriptional signatures are widely used as scalable surrogates for tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) in bulk tumour expression data. Using 438 patients from TCGA-HNSC and seven gene sets scored under three platform-agnostic algorithms, this study shows that (i) the three chemokine-based TLS signatures are nearly redundant with one another (Spearman rho >= 0.987); (ii) they correlate almost as strongly with a generic T cell-inflamed signature (rho = 0.89) as with each other; (iii) the consensus TLS score tracks checkpoint (rho = 0.898) and regulatory T cell (rho = 0.889) programmes far more strongly than the structural features of TLS, including germinal-centre B cells (rho = 0.462), plasma cells (rho = 0.496), and high endothelial venules (rho = 0.507); (iv) prognostically the score is cut-off dependent and not independent of stage and age (multivariable HR 0.757, 95% CI 0.463-1.238, p = 0.268), with discrimination (C-index 0.536) no better than a generic T cell-inflamed signature (0.546); and (v) HPV status does not confound the score's behaviour, although only 5 of 68 HPV-positive patients fall below the optimal cut-off, so a threshold-based chemokine score cannot discriminate within HPV-positive disease.

Contents. Fourteen numbered pipeline scripts (cohort construction from the Genomic Data Commons, three-algorithm gene set scoring, consensus score construction, internal validation, microenvironmental programme correlation, nomogram and decision curve analysis, HPV status determination from in situ hybridisation / p16 immunohistochemistry / pathology-report text with a nested leave-one-out transcriptomic classifier, and HPV-stratified survival analysis); gene set definitions; derived patient-level analysis tables; all result tables and figures; and pipeline run logs.

Licensing. Code is released under the MIT licence. Derived data and results are released under CC BY 4.0. Primary data are publicly available from the Genomic Data Commons under project TCGA-HNSC; no controlled-access or identifiable data were used.

Data handling note. Two GDC schema pitfalls that can silently corrupt a TCGA-HNSC cohort are handled explicitly: 172 of 528 participants carry more than one recorded diagnosis, so the analysis retains only the diagnosis flagged as primary disease with a squamous morphology code and a head-and-neck site of origin; and the deprecated field demographic.gender is replaced by demographic.sex_at_birth.

Known limitation. External validation cohorts (GSE65858, GSE159067) could not be retrieved in the analysis environment because NCBI/GEO was unreachable. The corresponding script is provided and ready to run; the reported findings should be regarded as discovery-only.
